_notes.readme: Draft. '_notes' is documentation for reviewers and is NOT part of the catalog schema (entries are strict): scripts/image-build.sh drops it from the filled entry, and it must not be copied into catalog.json.

runEnv.ROVARA_AWS_CONTROL_TOKEN: random per run; the run's own code never receives it. Without it every /_rovara/* path except /_rovara/health answers 403.
runEnv.QUARKUS_HTTP_HOST: the run IP literal of this container on the services network (for example 172.30.4.16); the emulator binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a wildcard such as 0.0.0.0.
runEnv.ROVARA_AWS_BASE_URL: http://aws:4566 (the run alias). With a token set the emulator refuses to start unless this is set and is not the development default.
runEnv.ROVARA_AWS_AUTH_PRESIGN_SECRET: random per run, 16 or more characters; the emulator refuses to start with a token set and this missing or default.
runEnv.ROVARA_AWS_SERVICES_SQS_RECEIPT_HANDLE_S: random per run, 16 or more characters; same rule.

_notes.health: GET /_rovara/health is open (no token). The catalog in Rovara still says /__rovara/health and must be fixed at merge.
_notes.memory: resources.memMiB 384 (Rovara catalog, 2026-11-03): the native gate measured 129 MiB total peak (39 MiB private) + the 64 MiB /tmp tmpfs + 128 MiB headroom for in-memory test data, rounded up. The ENTRYPOINT caps the heap with -Xmx192m so the Substrate VM default (a share of the container limit) cannot be OOM-killed; re-measure inside a 384 MiB container on staging.
_notes.platforms: The first image is linux/arm64 only (Rovara's workers are Graviton). scripts/image-build.sh writes the platforms it built into the filled entry; add linux/amd64 only if a customer needs it (the catalog then needs an index of exactly both).
